Title: The woman nobody got one past
Blurb: A description with no super in it. The interesting part is what the rulebook turns out not to have.

Turns.Speaker: person
Turns.Text: My gran ran the chip shop on the corner for forty years. Nobody ever got one past her and nobody ever laid a finger on her. I want to play her.

Turns.Speaker: assistant
Turns.Text: Two things and then I'll build her, and you can shrug at either. Street Level is the tier for people who are formidable rather than super, and I'll use it unless you want her bigger. And where does it come from — is she just like that, or is there a story behind it? I'll assume she's just like that.

Turns.Speaker: person
Turns.Text: Street's right. And no story, she's just like that. She'd be offended by the question.

Turns.Speaker: assistant
Turns.Text: Then here she is. One thing worth saying before you look: I went hunting for a Power that means "knows when you are lying" and the rulebook does not have one. That is not a hole in her — it is Perception and the Investigation Talent, both bought high, and at those ranks nobody gets one past her. The armour is the other half of what you said, and it starts from her Toughness rather than being bought from nothing.

Character.Name: Vera Nunn

Flaws.NarrativeDetail: The shop opens at eleven whatever else is happening
Two grandchildren who think she is just a nan

Character.Appearance: Seventy-one, an apron over a cardigan, forearms like a docker.
Character.Motivation: The corner is hers and she has never once said so out loud.
Character.Quote: Sit down. You'll have a cup of tea and then you'll tell me the truth.
Connections: Half the market, and the sergeant at the station who was in her Cubs

Turns.Speaker: assistant
Turns.Text: She comes in under the tier's budget rather than filling it, which for a character like this is the honest answer — there is nothing else she does. If you want the rest spent, her Toughness is where it would go, and the armour rises with it because it takes its baseline from that Ability.
